additions.site_name: Project Genesis Data Centre, 192 Narellan Road, Campbelltown
additions.name: 192 Narellan Road Data Centre (Project Genesis) — proposed 100 MW two-building data centre (SSD-150514738)

status.summary: On 21 October 2026 the NSW Department published MoreHuman Property Group's scoping report requesting SEARs for State significant development SSD-150514738, the 192 Narellan Road Data Centre (Project Genesis) on Lot 102 DP 1323758, Campbelltown: construction and 24/7 operation of a data centre of about 100 MW total load in two stages (a two-storey building up to 26 m and a three-storey building up to 30 m) within the site's northern E3 precinct. This supports an announced project only: SEARs have not been issued and no application, consent or site work exists.

locator.precision: Parent-property marker at the centroid of the 12.1 ha subject lot (Lot 102 DP1323758). Both proposed buildings and the substation are confined to the lot's roughly 5.9 ha northern E3 precinct; the marker does not locate either building, the substation, the entrance or the construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The scoping report gives the site as 192 Narellan Road, Campbelltown, legally Lot 102 in DP 1323758. The NSW cadastre returns exactly one polygon for that lot, and its outline matches 'The Site' on the report's zoning map. The NSW property register now addresses the same polygon as 180 Narellan Road (exact overlap) and gives 192 Narellan Road to an adjoining western property that does not intersect Lot 102, so identity rests on the legal lot and the matching outline, not on the street number. The portal's own point (150.7915, -34.0664, four decimals) falls in Lot 3098 DP1230014 south of Narellan Road, 272 m outside the subject lot, and is excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is a derived interior anchor of a lot about 490 by 470 m (farthest vertex 274 m), and the buildings' position within the northern precinct is not georeferenced.

additions.site_name: Road 1 Data Centre, 1-5 Khartoum Road, Macquarie Park
additions.name: Road 1 Data Centre — approved 49 MW data centre (SSD-80814238)

status.summary: On 1 October 2026 the Acting Director, Industry Assessments, as delegate of the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces, granted State significant development consent SSD-80814238 to Stockland Development Pty Ltd for the Road 1 Data Centre at 1-5 Khartoum Road, Macquarie Park (Part Lot 2 DP 1043041): construction and 24/7 operation of a ten-storey 49 MW (34.3 MW IT load) data centre with back-up generators, cooling plant, fuel and battery storage, part of Road 1 and Road 23, landscaping and earthworks. No construction, completion or operation is established.
status.permit_reference: NSW development consent SSD-80814238 (Road 1 Data Centre) under section 4.38 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, granted 1 October 2026 by the A/Director Industry Assessments as delegate of the Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (file EF25/3967); notice of decision and instrument published on the NSW Planning Portal on 2 October 2026
status.permit_identity_review: The notice of decision and the signed instrument both name SSD-80814238 Road 1 Data Centre, applicant Stockland Development Pty Ltd, site 1-5 Khartoum Road, Macquarie Park, Part Lot 2 DP 1043041, and approve construction and 24/7 operation of the 49 MW data centre itself (condition A6 caps total power consumption at 49 MW); the generators, roads and storage are parts of that approved development, not a separate ancillary permit. Condition A5 lapses the consent five years after it operates unless physically commenced. The separately determined 1-5 Khartoum Road Data Centre (SSD-63235720, determined 11 March 2026) and the adjoining Talavera Road Data Centre Campus (SSD-24299707) are different consents.

locator.precision: Parent-property marker at the centroid of the 4.12 ha former Lot 2 DP1043041, now Lots 20 and 21 DP1319168. The consented 8,096 m2 site occupies the lot's north-eastern portion fronting Murrell Street and future Road 1; the marker does not locate the building, the site boundary, the entrance or the construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The consent's site is Part Lot 2 DP 1043041 (1-5 Khartoum Road), which is no longer in the NSW cadastre. The assessment report lists LDA2024/0225, a subdivision of one lot into two, and describes Lot 2 as a battle-axe lot fronting Khartoum Road, Waterloo Road, Talavera Road and Murrell Street. Plan DP1319168 (registered in the cadastre on 1 September 2025) contains exactly two lots whose union is a battle-axe polygon of 4.12 ha (deed area of Lot 2: 4.076 ha) fronting exactly those four streets (centreline distances 6-14 m) and matching the outline of Lot 2 on the applicant's 2024 survey plan, so the union is taken as the former Lot 2. The portal's project point (151.123, -33.781; three decimals) lies on the road reserve 16 m outside the union at its western corner and is excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The cadastral service publishes no positional accuracy; the point is a derived interior anchor of a 4.12 ha battle-axe lot (farthest vertex 249 m) and the 8,096 m2 site's position within its north-eastern portion is not georeferenced; the link from Lot 2 DP1043041 to DP1319168 rests on the shape, area and four-street frontage match and the recorded one-into-two subdivision, not on a published plan-history record.
